  However, four defects invalidate parts of the decode and ALL of the lag
  stats; the claimed p50_s=0.0 is a measurement artifact, not evidence of
  speed:
  (D1) topic role misassignment. In all 2374 captured rows topic1 has
  non-zero upper 12 bytes — it is the orderHash, not an address. The probe's
  `maker` (last 20 bytes of topic1) is garbage for 100% of rows. True roles,
  confirmed in the validating receipt: topic2 = maker, topic3 = taker (the
  exchange address itself in the taker-summary log, e.g. topic3=0xe111...996b
  there). Registry matching still works because it checks topic2+topic3, but
  wallet attribution semantics are wrong.
  (D2) side derivation is broken: 2110/2374 rows side="", 264 BUY, zero SELL.
  Correct rule from the data words: word0==0 -> maker gave collateral -> BUY
  of asset word1, price=w2/w3, size=w3/1e6; word1==0 (word0=tokenId, 295 such
  rows captured) -> maker SOLD asset word0, price=w3/w2, size=w2/1e6. The
  current fixed price=w2/w3 formula returns 1/price for SELL-maker rows
  (~12% of the sample).
  (D3) receive-lag clamping: probe_polygon_orderfilled_ws.py:165 computes
  `max(0.0, recv - block_ts)`; 2011/2374 rows had recv < block_ts, so
  p50_s=0.0 just means "clamped". Polygon block timestamps are
  producer-stamped at 1s granularity and often at-or-ahead of wall clock;
  the signed value must be kept.
  (D4) lag stats commingle sources: the 200 polygon_http_getLogs backfill
  rows (received_at = fetch time, hence max_s=31.16) are averaged with the
  2174 WS rows. Stats must filter source=="polygon_ws".
  Also: validation used 1 tx where the direction ordered 5-10. Legacy 5-word
  decode absent but ZERO rows were captured on 0x4bFb/0xC5d5 — keep the
  address filters, leaving legacy undecoded is acceptable unless rows appear.

## 2026-07-04T10:35:00Z fable DIRECTION — COPY THE INVENTORY, NOT THE ORDER (LIVE, model change)
- audit (evidence, my own read of the raw wallet-events feed, last ~30MB):
  26 windows, 15,702 tracked-wallet events; orders per 5m window: min 4,
  p50 46, p90 2,062, max 4,370; zero in-window SELLs; accumulation at
  laddered prices (e.g. 0.49/0.45/0.15 in one window). The copied
  behavior is INVENTORY BUILDING, not discrete entries. The operator
  spotted this and is right; per-order 1:1 mirroring at $2/order against
  a 46-4,370 orders/window accumulator is the wrong execution frame and
  explains much of the fak_no_match race.
- ordered (live copy model v2 — window-inventory mirroring):
  1. Track per (wallet, window, outcome): running inventory shares and
     volume-weighted avg price from the realtime feed. Compute per-wallet
     properly (group by proxy wallet from raw), not feed-aggregate.
  2. Our target position per window = policy fraction x their running
     inventory, capped by policy USD. The intent becomes "converge to
     target position", not "mirror order X".
  3. Consolidation execution: submit FAK (maker fallback stays) whenever
     our position < target AND best ask <= their running VWAP + buffer
     (buffer from drift/edge as already wired). Batch converge on each
     guard cycle; the 3s freshness gate applies to the inventory state
     update, not to individual source orders — late individual events no
     longer matter, stale WINDOW state does.
  4. Late-window guard: stop converging when time-to-resolution < T
     (start T=60s, measure); their late adds are the most latency-toxic.
  5. A/B attribution: tag ledger rows copy_model=per_order|inventory;
     run inventory model as the live path, keep per-order rows readable
     for comparison. Named metrics: band fill rate, realized PnL per
     window vs their per-window PnL, avg copy price vs their VWAP
     (target: within +1 tick).
  6. CopyIntent parity and single guard unchanged — the intent payload
     gains inventory fields but the paper lane consumes the identical
     intents.
- expected effect: fill rate ceases to be a per-order race (p50 target
  >70% of target position converged per window), PnL tracks the wallet's
  window outcome minus a bounded avg-price slippage instead of losing a
  latency race 75% of the time.
- next: implement v2 behind fuse_hot_path guard, paper-validate one
  window set, reload, fresh decision window starts at reload ts (my
  10:20Z suspension logic applies to it).
- warnings: their max windows (4k orders) exceed any sane consolidation —
  cap our converge order count per window (policy) and let the target
  fraction do the sizing; never try to out-trade the firehose.

## 2026-07-04T15:20:00Z fable DIRECTION — WHALE-CONSENSUS SIGNAL LANE AUTHORIZED (operator-proposed): BACKTEST IT FROM EXISTING DATA THIS DAY
- audit: operator proposal, and it is sound: per window, read the
  AGGREGATE side the profitable leaderboard wallets are accumulating and
  build our own orders on that side. Advantages over 1:1 copy: no
  per-order latency race (aggregate flow is a seconds-scale signal),
  consensus of N proven wallets beats one wallet, and sizing/laddering is
  ours. This is the experimental lane from my 15:00Z entry, now concrete.
- design (lane: whale_consensus_v1):
  1. Signal: per (window, outcome), quality-weighted net accumulation of
     the top-K profile-positive wallets (weight = profile edge x recent
     PnL rank; K start 20). Trigger when weighted net crosses threshold S
     AND price of that side still <= P_max (edge not already priced in).
  2. Entry: ladder up to M orders on the consensus side below P_max,
     window-time guard (no entries in final 60s), hold to resolution.
  3. BACKTEST FIRST — no new captures, the data exists (polygon fill
     jsonls, CLOB snapshots, resolution rows): replay all captured
     windows; grid over S, P_max, entry-time buckets; output EV table
     per bucket with sample counts to
     data/research/whale_consensus_backtest_v1.json. This costs one
     heartbeat and decides the lane. Named decision: EV>0 in >=1 sizable
     bucket -> paper lane; EV<=0 everywhere -> lane killed, logged.
  4. If backtest passes: paper lane on live feed (same intents pipeline,
     copy_model=consensus tag), then standard promotion bar: beats
     incumbent lanes on measured PnL -> live via the single guard.
- priority: v2 fresh-window measurement (participation table + band
  numbers) stays first this heartbeat; the backtest rides the same or
  next heartbeat — it is offline compute, it does not touch live.
- warnings: survivor-bias guard in the backtest — select the top-K
  wallets using only information available BEFORE each replayed window
  (rolling profile), never the full-period ranking, or the EV table lies.
